method_system.caption: Task and controller schematic (not to scale). A rectangular part is pushed toward a target pose. At each 0.1 s control interval, the current 10-D state and candidate commands form the 11-D model input; a learned state-delta model recursively evaluates 128 five-step action sequences. When the current pose is outside tolerance, a fixed cost and validity checks select the first command. When the actual position and orientation are within tolerance, planning is bypassed and a common, nonlearned supervisor applies zero command; low actual speed and continuous 0.3 s qualification are checked at physics substeps. Future simulator states are not queried by planning.
method_system.nature: Explanatory schematic, not empirical scene image or measured trajectory

fixed_prediction.caption: Offline fixed-action position prediction on the 12 geometric-controller traces. Each point is the mean of 12 equally weighted family means, not the pooled-window mean. At K=1,5,10, respectively, all 2,656, 2,608, and 2,548 truth-eligible windows are valid for both methods in each plotted seed. Seed 11 is omitted because validity masks differ. Overlapping windows are not independent; these descriptive prediction errors do not establish closed-loop handoff improvement.
